This was a childhood favorite for me so it was kind of a hard watch looking past the rose-tinted glasses as not only an older viewer, but also as someone who does still deeply love classic Simpsons. The jokes that I remember still hit today, but a lot were trying to land off the idea of finding Homer’s horrible personality in this movie to be funny. It just wasn’t. In the way that The Spongebob Movie is often referred to as the last piece of good classic Spongebob, I feel The Simpsons Movie is a weird science experiment of classic Simpsons and modern Simpsons comedy that blends together in a strange new form that doesn’t work for me as it once did as a child who just saw “The Funny Yellow Family”. There are remnants of what made The Simpsons so good for me even today here. Theres pieces of genuine heartfelt moments that you’d find in the golden era, but you have to trudge through the off characterization and unfunny jokes that Homer is just the worst but will eventually be forgiven because he’s the main man. I don’t like it, it feels bad.

His lovable juvenile character from early seasons is dumbed down to that of an knit-witted moron whose actions range from stupid to down right evil, poisoning the towns water supply and fleeing to Alaska. If I was Marge (Simpson) I would have left that yellow glutton long ago. The rest of the cast isn’t much better with Bart being naked on my tv not being very funny, actually quite the opposite. The saving grace is the animation and visuals which still not amazing are definitely a step up from the show.

Why yes, I CAN believe this had 11 freaking writers, because this feels like 11 different people’s view as to what the Simpsons are, and none of them mesh in a way that makes more than four moments of this any good. Like, it’s weird how much this feels like Simpsons fanfic, despite being done by 11 separate showrunners; these are all people who know Springfield pretty intimately, and so it’s extra heartbreaking that they managed to make something that feels more like A Very Special Episode of the show than anything the show has ever done. And yes, I get that they had to shoehorn a decades-long show into 90 minutes, but making this weirdly serious — separation! parental drama! Unresolved mystery! — feels like a colossal miscalculation and a betrayal of everything the Simpsons are so that they can make this feel justified as a movie. Worse, it feels like they don’t even get the characters. For example, Homer is just the dumbest, most random, most insufferable version of himself that’s ever existed, and there’s almost no line here that feels organic; it’s all [INSERT HOMER SAYING SOMETHING AGGRESSIVELY RANDOM AND UNKNOWINGLY HARMFUL] over and over, and there’s no effort to tie it into explanations as to why he’s suddenly just like this evil random gas leak version of himself. Again, I found maybe three or four of the gags to be kinda funny, and they all feel like Monorail-era level of quality. The rest feel like “ha ha we showed Bart’s dong” or “ha ha Homer flips the bird” or just oddly disconnected beats too lazy to be any good. This was a huge bummer even if it did give us the meme-era gold of “this was the worst day of your life SO FAR.” The rest? Oof.

This movie was nothing more than a fleecing. The "Spider-Pig" thing was not that funny. And at the beginning of the movie... sigh... Look,  just because Homer makes a joke about paying to see a crappy movie in the theaters that they can see for free on TV as a show and getting ripped off by it doesn't make it okay that that's exactly what the audience for The Simpons has done. Anyone who saw The Simpsons in the theater paid to see something they usually get for free on TV - a mediocre Simpsons episode. If you jump to the big screen, I want to hear language you can't hear on TV, I want celebrity cameos out the wazoo, and I want every character from the show to make an appearance (criteria which The Simpsons movie fails to meet on each count). Homer's preemptive strike of a joke does not negate the fleecing. It simply feels like Groening & Co is calling everyone in the audience a sucker. I was one of those suckers. (originally published in The Mobtown Shank, 2007)

I was selected to lead, not to read Last Watch: September 2020 Age: 51 (at time of release) Source: Disney+ 2026 Challenge: Hanks at 70 Film: #38 Director/Cast/Premise The Simpsons Movie is the 2007 animated comedy directed by David Silverman. Starring Dan Castellaneta, Nancy Cartwright and Tom Hanks the plot sees the residents of Springfield imprisoned under a glass dome. Original Thoughts 2020 Things have a habit of following trends. When your career starts to develop as an actor you get more involved in the production of films, maybe set up your own company. If you have a tv show that becomes popular you end up making a film version. South Park did it in 1999, The Simpsons did it in 2007, is it necessary? No. Was the Simpsons movie worth it? Not really. The reality is that the film was a huge financial success but suffers from a number of expected problems; there are clear pacing issues that is most likely due to the inexperience of putting out anything beyond a normal episode run time, plenty of padding which is often dull and the material/character arcs that offer nothing new from its hundreds of available episodes with far too few jokes. There is a clear over reliance of the audiences fondness for the characters. Its these viewers who paid to watch an extended version of an episode and who the studio banked on making this a success. What you get is familiarity of the Springfield setting and Simpsons regulars with the odd cameo (Tom Hanks included) and sharper animation. For good measure they throw in some themes of religion and the environment whilst ripping off Stephen Kings Under the Dome. Oh and throw in a pig...it just isn't worth it.
